blocks.html: This is for an owner or operations lead at a team of roughly five to fifty people who keeps answering the same questions, and who knows the next hire will ask them again.
Any of these tools will hold documents. What separates them is how fast you can capture a process, how much it costs as the team grows, and whether you can see the price before talking to sales.

Start with Whale if you want to try it free and record processes as you do them. Pick Waybook if you want a published price and unlimited documents on every plan. Pick Trainual if you want training paths, roles, and SOPs in one system and don't mind getting a quote.
Whichever you choose, document the five tasks that new hires ask about most before buying anything. If you can't write those five, the tool won't do it for you.

Trainual offers Core, Pro, Premium, and Enterprise plans. It's priced by team size and features through a demo, with no public price. It includes 500+ free templates for processes, policies, roles, and responsibilities, a built-in screen recorder, plus flowcharts and embedded video, and AI-powered knowledge search with Q&A on every plan.
If you need to step back, an account can go on hold for up to three months instead of canceling. That's a useful option for a seasonal business.

Whale's Free plan is free forever for 1 creator, up to 10 members, and 20 Playbook items. Scale is $299 a month billed yearly, with 3 creators included, and extra creators cost $29 a month billed yearly, or $39 billed monthly, per extra creator. Advance is $599 a month billed yearly, with 5 creators included. Per Whale, yearly billing saves 25%.
The capture piece is the draw: Whale includes a screen recorder and a video-to-SOP converter, even on Free. Record a task once, then edit the steps it writes instead of starting from a blank page.

Waybook Core is $99 a month on annual billing, or $119 on monthly billing, plus $5 a month per additional member on annual billing. Pro is $198 a month on annual billing, or $238 on monthly billing, plus $10 a month per additional member on annual billing. There's a 7-day free trial, and annual billing saves 17%.
Waybook includes unlimited subjects, documents, and steps on every plan and an unlimited AI content writer on every plan. The per-member charge is the number to model as you grow.
Decide who writes. If one person documents everything, a plan priced by creator is cheap. If every team lead writes their own SOPs, a plan priced by member or by team size is easier to predict.
Then decide how processes get captured. Screen recording suits software tasks. Written steps with photos suit physical tasks. Most teams need both, so test each tool on one of each.
Last, look at what happens when someone leaves. The tool should make it obvious which documents that person owned so someone else can pick them up.
Pick one role, list its recurring tasks, and write those first. A finished set for one role beats a half-finished set for every role.
Set a review date on each document. Processes change, and a stale SOP does more harm than a missing one.
